lines: Take {gift_item}. I may not have a trade, but I know how to say thanks.
Here, {gift_item}. Maybe one of us will find the perfect use for it.
Take {gift_item}. It is not much, but it is given with care.
Most days, I am at the village square, trying to keep finding a calling from becoming everyone else's problem.
People think watching is simple until something goes wrong and suddenly it is very important.
A village runs on small work. Nobody praises it until it stops happening.
I trust a good empty hands more than a loud promise. The empty hands has less to prove.
If you want my honest answer, slow down first. Rushed questions usually hide worse ones.
The village looks calm from a distance. Up close, it is mostly chores arguing with weather.
I notice the little things. That is either a skill or what the village square has done to me.
Good, {gift_item} worked. See? I can be useful without a workstation.
{tested_villager} liked it? Excellent. I am putting that under possible talents.
Good. {gift_item} suited {tested_villager}; I like advice that holds up.
Following you taught me that plans sound much safer before anyone starts walking.
I kept up, mostly. My feet have a harsher opinion of the trip.
Next time, warn me before the road becomes a test of character.
I learned two things out there: stay close, and ask better questions earlier.
You move like danger is a normal part of the route. I am still adjusting to that.
It was not all bad. Some views are worth sore legs and nervous glances.
If I followed you again, I would pack more food and fewer assumptions.
Ah. Then my career in advice pauses here. Try {alternative_gift} for {gift_subject}.
{gift_item} was wrong? Let us call it research. {alternative_gift} should work better.
{gift_item} missed the mark for {gift_subject}. Try {alternative_gift} instead.

You walk in like trouble forgot to close the door behind it.
I have seen broken watching with better instincts than you.
Careful. The village has long memories and very little patience today.
You are not as frightening as you think. That may be the problem.
If foolishness made noise, you would drown out the bell.
